'''Josef Svoboda''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|CM}} (16 July 1929 – 21 November 2022) was a Canadian [[Arctic]] tundra scientist and botanist, who was appointed an Officer of the [[Order of Canada]] (2019) for his pioneering scientific contributions regarding the Arctic tundra ecosystems, and his lifelong mentorship of scientists.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://nunatsiaq.com/stories/article/five-people-with-ties-to-nunavut-nunavik-named-to-order-of-canada/|title=Five people with ties to Nunavut, Nunavik named to Order of Canada|date=2019-12-30|website=Nunatsiaq News|language=en|access-date=2020-01-01}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gg.ca/en/media/news/2019/governor-general-announces-120-new-appointments-order-canada|title=Governor General Announces 120 New Appointments to the Order of Canada|last=General|first=Office of the Secretary to the Governor|date=2019-12-20|website=The Governor General of Canada|access-date=2020-01-01}}</ref> He was an emeritus professor at the [[University of Toronto Mississauga]].

== Early life ==
Svoboda was born in [[Prague]], Czechoslovakia on 16 July 1929,<ref name="memory">{{Cite web|url=https://www.memoryofnations.eu/en/svoboda-josef-1929#biography|title = Josef Svoboda (1929)}}</ref> and raised in [[Moravia]] (in the [[Czech Republic]]).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.catholicregister.org/features/arts/item/27008-a-biologist-s-epic-tale-from-a-communist-regime-to-the-canadian-arctic|title=A biologist's epic tale from a Communist regime to the Canadian Arctic|last=Special|first=Geoffrey Woollard, A. Catholic Register|website=catholicregister.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2020-01-01}}</ref> His father was a locomotive engineer.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.radio.cz/en/section/one-on-one/josef-svoboda-from-uranium-mine-prison-labourer-to-arctic-ecologist-1|title=Josef Svoboda – From uranium mine prison labourer to Arctic ecologist|website=Radio Prague International|date=2 September 2013 |language=en|access-date=2020-01-01}}</ref> Svoboda survived [[World War II]], and developed an early love for nature by his Scout leader.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite book|title=Wine from raisins : a life transformed through Communist gulag to Canadian Arctic|last=Svoboda, J. (Josef)|isbn=978-2-89688-388-2|location=Toronto, Ontario|oclc=1035317929|date = September 2017}}</ref> He graduated from high school in 1948, and then began studying biology and philosophy at [[Masaryk University]] in 1948.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.catholicregister.org/features/featureseries/item/12667-finding-the-sacred-in-the-tundra|title=Finding the sacred in the tundra|last=Staff|first=Catholic Register|website=catholicregister.org|access-date=2020-01-01}}</ref>

While in university, Svoboda's involvement in student underground politics prompted his arrest at the age of 20, where he spent almost nine years in various prisons and labour camps, including being forced to work in a [[uranium]] mine for four years.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> While incarcerated, Svoboda continued to learn from fellow prisoners, and even received seminary training from bishops and prelates in a [[Leopoldov]] prison, though he was never ordained.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> Upon release in 1958, Svoboda attempted to continue his university studies with little success before taking on a research role at the Academy of Science in [[Brno]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4" />

== Research career ==
In the [[Prague Spring]] of 1968, at the age of 39, Svoboda left for [[Canada]] to complete a Bachelor of Science degree at the [[University of Western Ontario]], a doctorate at the [[University of Alberta]], and then began a 22-year-long teaching and research career at the [[University of Toronto]]'s Erindale College (now known as the [[University of Toronto Mississauga]]).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /> Since 1973, Svoboda has been studying the Arctic plant ecosystem in [[Nunavut]] and other parts of northern Canada.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" /> From 1992 and onwards, Svoboda's research lab has participated in the International Tundra Experiment to understand the timing and abundance of various Arctic flowers across different sites in relation to [[global warming]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.utm.utoronto.ca/biology/people/svoboda-josef|title=Svoboda, Josef {{!}} Biology|website=utm.utoronto.ca|access-date=2020-01-01|archive-date=2020-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200101231257/https://www.utm.utoronto.ca/biology/people/svoboda-josef|url-status=dead}}</ref>  In 1993, Svoboda received a Northern Science Award from the [[Polar Knowledge Canada]] in recognition of his contributions to the global understanding of plant communities following glacial retreat, and his pioneering approaches in Arctic [[botany]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.canada.ca/en/polar-knowledge/fundingforresearchers/awards/josef-svoboda.html|title=Josef Svoboda|date=2015-12-29|website=canada.ca|access-date=2020-01-01}}</ref>

Svoboda was later an [[emeritus]] professor of biology at the University of Toronto Mississauga.<ref name=":6" /> He recounted his life, from a Communist regime to the Canadian Arctic, in a 2017 autobiography titled: ''Wine from Raisins, A Life Transformed through Communist Gulag to Canadian Arctic.''<ref name=":4" /> He was appointed an Officer of the [[Order of Canada]] in 2019.<ref name=":1" />

== Personal life and death ==
In 1964 Svoboda married Kveta Krivkova, the sister of a fellow prisoner, who emigrated to Canada with him in 1968. They separated in 1973 when she returned to Czechoslovakia.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=Paul |title=Czech-Canadian scientist Josef Svoboda helped uncover secrets of the Arctic |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-czech-canadian-scientist-josef-svoboda-helped-uncover-secrets-of-the/ |website=The Globe and Mail |access-date=8 November 2024 |date=15 December 2022}}</ref>

Svoboda died on 21 November 2022, at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite web |title=Josef Svoboda O.C. |url=https://www.smithsfh.com/memorials/josef-svoboda-oc/5079536/index.php |website=Smith's Funeral Homes |access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

==Legacy==
The [[Czech Republic|Czech]] ''Josef Svoboda'' Arctic Research Station, is based in [[Longyearbyen]]. The station is the property of the [[University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice]]. It also provides facilities for scientists, researchers, and students from the [[Czech University of Life Sciences Prague]], the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]], and all over the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research communities |url=https://www.forskningsradet.no/en/svalbard-science-forum/svalbard-research-planning/research-communities/ |access-date=2022-03-21 |website=forskningsradet.no |language=en}}</ref><ref name="prf.jcu.cz/cars/ref">{{cite web |title=The station cooperates with many research organizations, for example:|url=https://www.prf.jcu.cz/cars/reference.html |website=prf.jcu.cz|publisher=Faculty of Science, University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice|access-date=28 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220107090608/https://www.prf.jcu.cz/cars/reference.html |archive-date=2022-01-07 |language=cs}}</ref><ref name="prf.jcu.cz/cars">{{cite web |title=Česká arktická výzkumná stanice |url=https://www.prf.jcu.cz/cars |website=prf.jcu.cz|publisher=Faculty of Science, University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice|access-date=28 June 2026}}</ref>
